title: Scalio: Scaling up DPU-based JBOF Key-value Store with NVMe-oF Target Offload
problem: Scaling distributed key-value stores in JBOF architectures faces CPU bottlenecks from NVMe-oF target-side processing. Current designs waste CPU cycles on storage protocol operations, limiting throughput and scalability.
motivation: Efficient CPU utilization is critical for scaling distributed key-value systems that must handle high I/O workloads without proportional CPU overhead.
method: Scalio offloads NVMe-oF target processing to Data Processing Units (DPUs) instead of CPUs. The DPU handles storage protocol operations, data movement, and target-side NVMe-oF logic, liberating CPU resources for application workloads. This architecture reduces CPU overhead through hardware specialization for I/O-intensive operations across JBOF nodes.
key_novelty: Offloading NVMe-oF target functionality to DPUs to eliminate CPU bottlenecks in JBOF-based key-value store scaling.
contributions: DPU-based NVMe-oF target offload architecture for distributed key-value stores
CPU resource liberation and improved scalability through hardware-based protocol offload
Demonstration of efficient JBOF scaling with reduced per-node CPU footprint
limitations: Specific performance metrics, baseline comparisons, and detailed evaluation methodology are not discussed based on title analysis alone.
